back: Planning and controlling resource use and human activities to protect the environment for present and future generations.
Pristine: still in its natural state. Degraded: quality reduced by human activity (erosion, pollution, mining).
Sacred sites, taboos, totems and rules enforced by chiefs that protected trees, water and animals.
Environmental Management Agency, set up under the Environmental Management Act (Chapter 20:27): EIAs, pollution licences, fines.
Manage water under the Water Act; seven catchments: Gwayi, Manyame, Mazowe, Mzingwane, Runde, Sanyati, Save.
ZimParks: national parks and wildlife (Parks and Wild Life Act). Forestry Commission: state forests and timber (Forest Act).
Turning an international agreement into national law so that it can be enforced at home.
Ramsar 1971 (wetlands), CITES 1973 (wildlife trade), Montreal 1987 (ozone), Basel 1989 and Bamako 1991 (hazardous waste), UNFCCC 1992, Kyoto 1997.

front: Why environmental laws are hard to enforce
back: Few staff and funds, low fines, poverty and lack of alternatives, overlapping mandates, corruption, low awareness.
